messages:
ashley (acct-exec): Hey team — urgent POC blocker. Customer integration sometimes receives extra trailing bytes appended after the JSON when using function-calling + json_mode. Their client JSON.parse fails intermittently. Can we swarm?

sam (sales-engineer): Do we have a sample response and whether they used streaming?

ashley (acct-exec): They pasted this:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  \"choices\": [{\"message\": {\"name\": \"extract\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"id\\\": 123, \\\"items\\\": [\\\"a\\\", \\\"b\\\"]}\"}}]
}
--binary-leftover--
```
They said model=redwood-medium-v1, streaming=false, max_tokens=512, and they do client retries on 500/429. Also saw a 429 with X-Request-Id: req_9b2f.

tyler (ml-eng): Two asks: full request ids for the errors, and whether they reuse connections (keep-alive) or use gzip/chunked. If they retry on the same connection while we are still finishing a previous response it can concatenate bytes.

prashant (infra): Agree. If client retries early and the worker hasn't flushed a delimiter, TCP stream could contain leftover bytes. Ops-bot, pull traces for req_9b2f.

ops-bot: Trace available: https://internal.traces/replay/req_9b2f. Related spans: req_9b2f, req_9b2g.

tyler (ml-eng): That matches a pattern we've seen in staging. Ask customer for the raw HTTP payload including headers. In parallel we'll look at worker logs.

sam (sales-engineer): Customer also wants a short note on pricing impact if they disable aggressive client retries in favor of SDK-level dedupe.

prashant (infra): Quick line: aggressive retries can double token spend when retries repeat successful or partial responses. With 10% retry rate expect up to ~10% extra token usage; using idempotency keys and SDK de-dup mitigates this.

ashley (acct-exec): They also asked about log retention for security questionnaire — will we retain prompt+response?

prashant (infra): For Dedicated you can control retention and disable prompt logging. Hosted can be restricted under enterprise contract. I'll loop in compliance for POC specifics.

tyler (ml-eng): Ops-bot, any worker-side warnings?

ops-bot: Correlated ids -> worker-22 (gpu-a100-3). WARN at 2026-03-19T14:12:05Z: "stream-terminate: leftover-bytes".

tyler (ml-eng): That WARN is likely the cause. Short-term mitigations to give the customer: 1) enable streaming=true and parse as a stream; 2) add a defensive sanitizer that extracts the first JSON object before JSON.parse; 3) upgrade to SDK with request de-dup.

sam (sales-engineer): Can we provide a tiny SDK/snippet for Node to sanitize responses while we triage?

prashant (infra): Here's a quick Node helper (for triage only):
```js
async function safeParse(respText) {
  // naive: find end of first JSON object by matching the last closing brace before non-whitespace
  const idx = respText.indexOf('\n--'); // heuristics for trailing marker in their sample
  const payload = idx === -1 ? respText : respText.slice(0, idx).trim();
  return JSON.parse(payload);
}
```

tyler (ml-eng): I'll prepare a hotfix: append an explicit delimiter ("\n---\n") to JSON-mode responses from the worker shim so concatenation is detectable. Plan: patch + unit tests (1-2h), staging run (2h), canary 10% (2h), full rollout next maintenance window.

sam (sales-engineer): ETA question from customer?

ashley (acct-exec): I'll tell them hotfix in staging today, canary tomorrow, production rollout asap pending no regressions. Offer the SDK sanitizer and Dedicated retention controls as interim. Also schedule a 17:00 PT call to walk through.

tyler (ml-eng): After rollout we'll add integration tests simulating retries with keep-alive connections to prevent regressions and cover streaming vs non-streaming behavior.

ashley (acct-exec): Thanks all — will post the raw HTTP payload and the customer's retry pattern when they send it. :thumbsup:
